join_order.notes: 29,997 movie_link rows total; sequel/follows/followed by typically cover most rows. Linear scan of link_type_id column, keep rows where in set. Yields surviving ml rowids with their movie_id and linked_movie_id.
t2.id = ml.linked_movie_id; title is dimension PK so title row position == id-1 (or use pos index). Read t2.production_year[id]: must be in [2000,2010]. Then t2.kind_id must be in kt_allowed_ids.
t1.id = ml.movie_id. Read t1.kind_id: must be in kt_allowed_ids.

For each surviving t2.id, iterate movie_info_idx rows in [off[id], off[id+1]); keep where info_type_id == it_rating_id AND info < '3.5'. Must have at least one match. Track lex-min of info as second_rating.
For each surviving t1.id, iterate movie_info_idx rows in [off[id], off[id+1]); keep where info_type_id == it_rating_id. Must have at least one match. Track lex-min of info as first_rating.

For each surviving t1.id, iterate mc rows; for each, look up cn1 via company_name__id__pos[company_id]; keep where cn1.country_code != '[us]'. Must have at least one match. Track lex-min of cn1.name as first_company. Track lex-min of t1.title as first_movie.

For each surviving t2.id, iterate mc rows; cn2 has no country_code filter. Just require at least one mc2 row exists. Track lex-min of cn2.name (via company_name__id__pos[company_id]) as second_company. Track lex-min of t2.title as second_movie.

data_structures.agg_state: six std::string running-min slots (or string_view tracked + final copy)

parallelism.reduction: per-thread local min strings, final merge picks lex-min across threads
parallelism.notes: movie_link is small (~30k rows); split linearly across 12 threads. Each thread does all downstream probes for its slice. Merge 6 MIN aggregates at end.

indexes.purpose: id->row for t1, t2 attribute reads
only for literal resolution scan (linear scan acceptable, table has 113 rows)

execution_notes: Driver choice rationale: movie_link is by far the smallest fact table relevant here (~30k rows), and it transitively constrains BOTH t1 and t2 ids. Driving on movie_link avoids enumerating all ~2.5M title rows.
All movie_id-keyed facts (movie_info_idx, movie_companies) use their primary CSR for O(matches) range scans per t1.id and t2.id, which is optimal given the physical sort order.
The join condition 'ml.movie_id = mi_idx1.movie_id = mc1.movie_id' (and similarly for t2 side) is automatically satisfied by joining all three to t1.id (resp. t2.id) — no extra equality check needed.
Since aggregation is unconditional MIN with no GROUP BY, no early-exit is safe; must scan all surviving rows.

For each ml row we need: at least one matching mi_idx1 (rating), at least one matching mi_idx2 (rating, <3.5), at least one matching mc1 (non-us), at least one matching mc2 (any). All four are existential semi-joins gating the row's contribution; the MINs use the lex-smallest qualifying value seen.
